topic: Knowledge-Inbox Review 2026: Local-First Knowledge Ingestion for AI Agents and Obsidian

key_points: Local-first knowledge ingestion for Obsidian and other local retrieval tools; turns links, text, videos, screenshots, PDFs, and local files into structured Markdown knowledge cards
Harness-neutral: Hermes, Codex, OpenClaw, and other MCP clients share the same adapters and processing service
Supports 12 source types: web pages, WeChat Official Accounts, X/Twitter, YouTube, podcast RSS/Apple Podcasts, Vimeo, direct media/HLS, PDF, images, audio/video, WeChat Channels, Telegram
Pipeline: source adapter -> ContentItem -> Cleaner/OCR/Whisper/AI -> Classifier/Tags/Knowledge Linker -> Obsidian Markdown + SQLite
MCP server (scripts/knowledge_mcp.py) exposes knowledge_ingest, knowledge_get_job, knowledge_list_capabilities
OpenAI-compatible AI layer (works with local Ollama), AI disabled by default with local fallback summary
Knowledge linking uses qmd or falls back to lexical matching over latest 1,000 notes; atomic card writes so indexers never see partial notes
Apache-2.0, Python 3.11+, FastAPI on port 8787, v0.3.0, created 2026-08-11, ~67 stars
WeChat Channels integration relies on separate ltaoo/wx_channels_download with its own security/license boundary
Official Obsidian Web Clipper browser extension for one-click page capture into a vault
Simple, first-party, no server needed — but limited to browser capture (no video/PDF/IM/social feeds)
Knowledge-Inbox's roadmap lists a browser extension for one-click desktop capture as a natural next client, not yet included
Self-hostable AI second brain; answers from web or docs with custom agents, automations, deep research
~36,400 GitHub stars — the dominant incumbent for AI-over-your-notes
AGPL-3.0, Python; heavier, broader scope than a focused ingestion tool
Focuses on retrieval/chatting over a knowledge base rather than a universal multi-source ingestion pipeline
Local-first LLM Wiki built on Karpathy's pattern: open-source knowledge graph builder, RAG knowledge base, agent memory store
~654 stars, MIT, TypeScript; positions as an Obsidian alternative rather than an ingestion layer for Obsidian
Aims to be durable Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw memory — competes on the knowledge-storage side
Knowledge-Inbox complements this pattern by feeding structured cards into an existing vault
Karpathy LLM Wiki pattern integrated into an Obsidian agentic workflow
28 HN points — shows demand for agent-maintained Markdown knowledge in Obsidian
Focuses on the agent-maintained wiki/retrieval side, less on universal capture from many source platforms
Complements Knowledge-Inbox which focuses on ingestion breadth

stats.fact: Knowledge-Inbox v0.3.0 supports 12 distinct source types (web, WeChat OA, X, YouTube, podcasts, Vimeo, HLS media, PDF, images, audio/video, WeChat Channels, Telegram) normalized into a single ContentItem
Khoj AI has ~36,473 GitHub stars as of Aug 2026, making it the leading self-hostable AI second brain
SwarmVault, a local-first LLM Wiki built on Karpathy's pattern, has ~654 stars and 28 HN points for agent-maintained Markdown knowledge, reflecting growing demand in this space
Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern has spawned multiple open-source implementations (wuphf with 260 HN points, CacheZero, LLMWiki.app), signaling an active ecosystem of local-first agent knowledge tools
Obsidian Web Clipper is the official first-party capture extension, but covers only browser page capture — leaving video, IM, social feeds, PDFs, and local files to tools like Knowledge-Inbox
Knowledge-Inbox is Apache-2.0 licensed, requires Python 3.11+, runs as FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8787, and uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so it works fully local with Ollama (e.g. qwen2.5:7b)

angles: Universal ingestion is the differentiator — one input box (paste URL, drop PDF, forward IM link) feeds a common AI classification/linking pipeline into Obsidian, unlike single-purpose clippers or retrieval-only second brains
Harness-neutral MCP design lets Hermes, Codex, and OpenClaw share the same adapters — the knowledge layer is decoupled from any one AI client
Local-first by default: AI disabled with a local fallback summary, optional Ollama backend, everything stored as plain Markdown + SQLite — no vendor lock-in or cloud dependency
Mobile capture via forwarding to Telegram/Discord/IM through an agent harness, filling the gap where web clippers and desktop tools don't reach
The WeChat Channels integration is a distinctive niche for Korean/Chinese-language content pipelines, but carries a security boundary worth calling out (separate downloader project, local TLS proxy)
Karpathy LLM Wiki pattern as the philosophical backdrop — agent-maintained Markdown knowledge is the emerging pattern, and ingestion is the missing front door
